boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Georgia customs, from North Campus rituals to Sanford Stadium pageantry.

cards.title: Ring the Chapel Bell
cards.subtitle: UGA Chapel Bell · North Campus
cards.notes: After a Georgia victory or a personal academic milestone, visit the Chapel Bell and join the long-running custom of ringing it.
cards.short_summary: A North Campus bell-ringing ritual for victories and milestones.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA says the Bulldog family rings the Chapel Bell for athletic victories, academic accomplishments, and other special occasions.
cards.access_notes: The bell is at the UGA Chapel in the heart of North Campus.

cards.title: Pose by the Arch
cards.subtitle: The Arch · North Campus
cards.notes: Use the Arch as a North Campus photo stop and take a moment to notice its three pillars: wisdom, justice, and moderation.
cards.short_summary: A campus-icon photo tradition at UGA’s gateway to downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA identifies the Arch as a popular campus photo spot, its official symbol, and the gateway between North Campus and downtown Athens.
cards.access_notes: Located at the north end of North Campus, entering from West Broad Street.

cards.title: Form the Power G
cards.subtitle: Freshman Welcome · Sanford Stadium
cards.notes: If you are a new Bulldog, attend Freshman Welcome, learn the school cheers, and join classmates in forming the Power G for a field photo.
cards.short_summary: New students create a giant Power G at Sanford Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA says Freshman Welcome is held before the first day of classes and has the incoming class form the Power G on Sanford Stadium’s field.
cards.access_notes: Annual event for the newest UGA class, hosted the day before classes begin.

cards.title: Light Up Sanford
cards.subtitle: Sanford Stadium · Fourth quarter of night games
cards.notes: At a night game’s fourth quarter, turn on your phone flashlight with the crowd as the Redcoat Band plays “Krypton Fanfare.”
cards.short_summary: Phone lights and stadium LEDs turn a fourth quarter into a shared display.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA says fans use phone flashlights at the start of the fourth quarter of night games while the Redcoat Band plays “Krypton Fanfare.”
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the fourth quarter of UGA night football games at Sanford Stadium.

cards.title: Sing “Glory, Glory”
cards.subtitle: UGA athletic events · Redcoat Band tradition
cards.notes: Follow along with “Glory, Glory” at an event; it is UGA’s fight song and has been sung at games since the 1890s.
cards.short_summary: UGA’s enduring fight-song tradition, set to “The Battle Hymn of the Republic.”
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Athletics calls “Glory, Glory” one of the university’s oldest and most lasting traditions and says it was sung at games as early as the 1890s.
cards.access_notes: Listen for the song at Georgia athletic events.

cards.title: Listen for the Lone Trumpeter
cards.subtitle: Sanford Stadium · Pregame
cards.notes: Arrive before kickoff to hear the lone trumpeter play the opening notes of “The Battle Hymn of the Republic” from the upper deck.
cards.short_summary: A solitary trumpet pregame cue at Sanford Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Athletics says a lone trumpeter plays the first 14 notes of “The Battle Hymn of the Republic” seven minutes before kickoff.
cards.access_notes: The pregame solo occurs seven minutes before kickoff in Sanford Stadium.

cards.title: See “Between the Hedges”
cards.subtitle: Sanford Stadium playing field
cards.notes: Look down to the Chinese privet hedge border around Sanford’s field and connect the landscape feature to UGA’s familiar home-field phrase.
cards.short_summary: The hedge-lined field behind UGA’s defining stadium nickname.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Athletics documents “Between the Hedges” as a reference to Sanford Stadium dating to the early 1930s and identifies the Chinese privet hedges around the field.
cards.access_notes: Visible around Sanford Stadium’s playing field during stadium access or events.

cards.title: Spot the Silver Britches
cards.subtitle: Georgia football uniform tradition
cards.notes: At a Georgia football game, look for the silver pants that give the Bulldogs’ “Silver Britches” tradition its visual signature.
cards.short_summary: A football-uniform nickname with a long UGA history.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Athletics says “Silver Britches” began under Coach Wally Butts and was reintroduced by Coach Vince Dooley in 1980.
cards.access_notes: Associated with Georgia football uniforms at games and team appearances.

cards.title: Close Commencement with the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: UGA commencement ceremonies
cards.notes: At commencement, stay through the closing Alma Mater; it formally signals the end of each University of Georgia graduation exercise.
cards.short_summary: UGA’s ceremonial closing song for graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Commencement states that singing the University of Georgia Alma Mater signals the end of each commencement exercise.
cards.access_notes: Part of University of Georgia commencement exercises.

cards.entity_name: Georgia On My Mind at Commencement
cards.title: Hear “Georgia on My Mind” at Graduation
cards.subtitle: Undergraduate commencement ceremony
cards.notes: At undergraduate commencement, listen for the student performance of “Georgia on My Mind,” selected to celebrate the graduating class.
cards.short_summary: A student-performed graduation moment unique to UGA’s ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Commencement says a student is selected at each undergraduate commencement ceremony to sing “Georgia on My Mind” for the graduating class.
cards.access_notes: Presented at each University of Georgia undergraduate commencement ceremony.
